name: Medical Call Management SaaS
elevator: We are building a SaaS platform that helps doctors manage patient interactions through secure call recording, AI-powered summaries, and comprehensive patient record management.
description: SaaS tool for doctors to record, summarize, and manage patient calls.

current_prd.elevator_pitch: SaaS tool for doctors to record, summarize, and manage patient calls.
current_prd.problem_statement: Doctors struggle with manual record-keeping and creating summaries of patient calls, leading to time waste and potential errors in patient care.
current_prd.solution: A comprehensive SaaS tool that provides secure call recording, AI-powered clinical summaries, patient record management, and role-based access control to streamline healthcare workflows.

key_features.feature_description: Securely record and store patient call audio.
Generate clinical summaries using transcript generation and GPT.
Create and view patient profiles, visit history, and call logs.
Role-based access control for physicians and staff.

target_audience.name: Doctors and Medical Staff
target_audience.pain_points: Time-consuming administrative tasks, difficulty accessing patient data quickly, and risk of data breaches.
target_audience.needs_and_goals: Efficiently manage patient information, streamline workflows, and improve patient care.

phasing.rationale: This phase includes the core functionalities required for a basic, launch-able product. It allows doctors to record calls, manage patient records, and ensures secure access.
This phase adds the AI-powered summaries feature to enhance the functionality of the MVP. It can be launched as an update to the MVP.

current_prd.design_principles: Security, Simplicity, Efficiency, and Accessibility. The design prioritizes data protection while maintaining an intuitive user experience for healthcare professionals.

steps.description: Starts call recording within the application
Records the audio and securely stores the file

user_journeys.context: Doctor records a patient call for documentation and analysis

steps.description: Generates transcript and clinical summary using AI
Accesses the call recording from patient record
Edits or adds notes to the summary

user_journeys.context: Doctor reviews AI-generated summary of a patient call

steps.description: Searches for a patient by name or ID
Displays patient profile, visit history, and call logs
Reviews patient information and updates records if necessary

user_journeys.trigger: Doctor needs to access patient history

current_prd.sitemap:
Dashboard
-> Patient Records
  -> Patient Profile
  -> Visit History
  -> Call Logs
-> Call Recording
-> AI Summaries
-> Access Control
-> Settings
current_prd.navigation_design: The application uses a top navigation bar for main sections (Dashboard, Patient Records, Call Recording, AI Summaries, Access Control, Settings). Patient Records has sub-navigation for Patient Profile, Visit History, and Call Logs. A prominent search bar is available on all pages for quick patient lookup.
current_prd.schema: The data model includes tables for Users, Patients, CallLogs, Recordings, and Summaries.  Users table stores user credentials and roles. Patients table stores patient information. CallLogs table stores metadata about each call. Recordings table stores the audio files. Summaries table stores the AI-generated summaries of the calls.

rows.value: Patient reports chest pain and shortness of breath.

user_stories.title: Record Patient Calls

user_story.so_that: I can accurately document the consultation and review it later

acceptance_criteria: Given I am logged in as a doctor, when I initiate a call with a patient, then I have the option to start recording the call
Given I start recording, when the call ends, then the audio file is securely stored and associated with the patient's record
Given I am not logged in as a doctor, when I try to record a call, then the system prevents me from doing so

user_stories.title: Generate AI-Powered Summaries

user_story.i_want: to have AI-powered summaries of patient calls
user_story.so_that: I can quickly review the key information from each consultation

acceptance_criteria: Given a call recording exists, when the system processes the recording, then a transcript is generated
Given a transcript is generated, when the AI model analyzes the transcript, then a clinical summary is created
Given a clinical summary is created, when I view the call details, then I can see the transcript and the summary

user_stories.title: Manage Patient Records

user_story.so_that: I can easily access and update patient information

acceptance_criteria: Given I am logged in as a doctor, when I search for a patient, then I can view their profile, visit history, and call logs
Given I have the necessary permissions, when I access a patient record, then I can create and update their information
Given I don't have the necessary permissions, when I try to access a patient record, then I am denied access

user_stories.title: Secure Access Control

user_story.i_want: to have secure access control to patient records
user_story.so_that: patient data is protected and only authorized personnel can access it

acceptance_criteria: Given I am an authenticated user, when I try to access patient records, then I am granted access based on my role and permissions
Given I am not an authenticated user, when I try to access patient records, then I am denied access
Given I am an authenticated user, but do not have permission to view a specific record, when I try to access it, then I am denied access

planned.model_content:
class Patient < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :organization
  belongs_to :creator, class_name: 'User'
  has_many :call_logs, dependent: :destroy

  rhino_owner :organization
  rhino_references [:organization, :creator]

  validates :name, presence: true
  validates :dob, presence: true
end
planned.migration_content:
class CreatePatients < ActiveRecord::Migration[7.2]
  def change
    create_table :patients do |t|
      t.string :name, null: false
      t.string :dob, null: false
      t.references :organization, null: false, foreign_key: true
      t.references :creator, null: false, foreign_key: { to_table: :users }

      t.timestamps
    end
  end
end
planned.rails_model_generation_command_line: rails generate model Patient name:string dob:string organization:references creator:references

planned.model_content:
class CallLog < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :patient
  has_many :recordings, dependent: :destroy

  rhino_owner :patient
  rhino_references [:patient]

  validates :call_time, presence: true
end
planned.migration_content:
class CreateCallLogs < ActiveRecord::Migration[7.2]
  def change
    create_table :call_logs do |t|
      t.datetime :call_time, null: false
      t.references :patient, null: false, foreign_key: true

      t.timestamps
    end
  end
end
planned.rails_model_generation_command_line: rails generate model CallLog call_time:datetime patient:references

planned.model_content:
class Recording < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :call_log
  has_one :summary, dependent: :destroy
  has_one_attached :audio_file

  rhino_owner :call_log
  rhino_references [:call_log]

  validates :audio_file, presence: true
end
planned.migration_content:
class CreateRecordings < ActiveRecord::Migration[7.2]
  def change
    create_table :recordings do |t|
      t.references :call_log, null: false, foreign_key: true

      t.timestamps
    end
  end
end

planned.model_content:
class Summary < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :recording

  rhino_owner :recording
  rhino_references [:recording]

  validates :summary_text, presence: true
end
